sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that gemilus chasadim for the wealthy involves an influence from chesed that is above the level of wealth itself.

translations.translation: And the maamar continues,
that it is stated in the Gemara37
that tzedakah is for the poor and gemilus chasadim is both for the poor and for the wealthy.
From this
(that gemilus chasadim is also for the wealthy)
it is understood,
that the influence from the aspect of chesed is above the level of a wealthy person.
And to note,
that ostensibly one could say that the influence of chesed to a wealthy person is that they are granted a greater wealth than the wealth they had previously.
And what is said in the maamar, that the influence from the aspect of chesed is above the level of a wealthy person,
one could say,
that when the influence that is now granted to him is a matter that is commensurate with his level,
then,
since previously he lacked the matter that is being granted to him
(even though the matter is commensurate with his level),
he is not
(the true essence of the matter of)
a wealthy person.
Therefore the maamar explains,
that gemilus chasadim for the wealthy is that the abundance from the aspect of chesed is above the level of a wealthy person,
meaning that it is of an entirely different category
(and that it has no matter that is not commensurate with his level at all,
is not a deficiency in his wealth).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the ultimate wealth of Shlomo's era came from the revelation of the inner aspect of Kesser, drawing down extraordinary wealth both physically and spiritually.

translations.translation: And in order to explain the matter of chesed that is above wealth,
the maamar precedes with an explanation of the matter of the wealth that existed in the days of Shlomo
(the most elevated level of wealth).
And it explains,
that this, that in the days of Shlomo the moon stood in its perfection38,
is,
that in addition to the five partzufim that were drawn into Malchus
(the moon,
Sihra)
which had been lacking,
there was also drawn into it the revelation of the innerness of Kesser,
Atik.
And from the wealth of Malchus
(Knesses Yisrael)
extraordinary wealth was drawn down to Yisrael even below,
extraordinary wealth in physicality, to the point that silver was not considered anything in the days of Shlomo39,
and extraordinary wealth in spirituality,
that specifically in the days of Shlomo the Beis HaMikdash was built,
for the revelation that was in the Beis HaMikdash is a more elevated revelation than the revelation that was in the Mishkan that preceded it.
And to add,
that this, that in the days of Shlomo there was a most elevated revelation,
was even before the Beis HaMikdash was built.
For that the building of the Beis HaMikdash was specifically by Shlomo
[even though the design of the Temple was made by Dovid40]
is as it is stated41
He
(Shlomo)
will be a man of rest etc. and peace and quiet I will give upon Yisrael in his days
(and therefore)
he will build a house for My Name etc.,
and it is known,
that this, that all the nations were nullified to Shlomo
[therefore in his days there was rest and peace]
was that they were nullified to the revelation of Ein Sof that shone through him42.
And likewise regarding this, that they came to him from all the nations to hear his wisdom43,
the true reason for this, that they came to him, is because they were drawn to G-dliness
(and in the manner of what is stated44
regarding Moshiach45
and all the nations will stream to him,
that this, that everyone will be drawn to him, is that they will be drawn to G-dliness).
For the revelation of light that shone then,
drew to itself the sparks that were among the nations,
similar to a torch that draws all sparks to itself46.
And since the revelation that shone then was a most elevated revelation,
therefore,
even the sparks in the distant places47
were drawn to the revelation that shone through Shlomo,
as it is stated48
And the Queen of Sheba heard the fame of Shlomo for the Name of G-d etc. and she came to Yerushalayim etc.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contrasts the refinement through the Mishkan, which was through war, with the refinement through the Beis HaMikdash, which was through rest, and explains the true meaning of rest.

translations.translation: And behold, that Shlomo was a man of rest,
that the refinement in his days was in a manner of rest
[that there was no need for war in order to refine the sparks,
rather the sparks were drawn to him on their own,
to be refined],
this was primarily through the revelation that shone in the Beis HaMikdash.
For the refinement through the revelation that shone in the Mishkan,
including also the revelation that shone in the Ark that was in the Mishkan,
was in a manner of war,
and the refinement through the revelation that shone in the Beis HaMikdash was in a manner of rest.
As it is stated in the Zohar49,
There were two who said "Arise, Hashem",
Moshe and Dovid,
Moshe said50
"Arise, Hashem, and let Your enemies be scattered",
and Dovid said51
"Arise, Hashem, to Your resting place."
And it is explained in the maamar52,
that this, that the Mishkan and the Ark traveled in the desert in order to nullify the klipos that were in the desert
(snakes, serpents, and scorpions)
and to refine and elevate the sparks of holiness that had fallen there,
is a refinement in a manner of war.
Like a king who goes out from his place and goes to the enemy's country to fight him and conquer him.
Therefore Moshe said
[regarding the journeying of the Ark in the desert—"And it was, when the Ark journeyed"]
"Arise, Hashem, and let Your enemies be scattered",
for there are enemies that one must fight against.
And the refinement through the revelation that shone in the Beis HaMikdash was in a manner of rest,
for Shlomo was in his place and the sparks were drawn to him on their own.
Therefore Dovid said "Arise, Hashem, to Your resting place."
And to note,
that in many places53
it is explained,
that the refinement that was through the journeying of the Ark in the desert is a refinement in a manner of rest.
For the matter of rest that is explained there is that the refinement is in a spontaneous manner.
And since the nullification of the klipos and the refinement of the sparks that fell into them through the revelation that shone in the Mishkan was in a spontaneous manner,
therefore,
even the refinement through the Ark of the Mishkan is called a refinement in a manner of rest.
But the true matter of rest is that the one who refines does not descend to the place of that which is being refined, but rather remains in his place,
and through the revelation of light
(of the one who refines)
that shines upon that which is being refined,
it is drawn on its own to the one who refines.
And rest in this manner was specifically in the days of Shlomo.
[And in the manner of what is known54
regarding the matter of refinement through Torah,
that in general,
even the refinement through the revealed aspect of Torah is in a manner of rest.
For since the refinement is in a spontaneous manner
(for by learning Torah, that this thing is permitted and this thing is forbidden,
they are refined spontaneously.
And not like the refinement of prayer, which is through the G-dly soul clothing itself in the animal soul),
therefore,
even the refinement through the revealed aspect of Torah is called a refinement in a manner of rest.
But in particular,
since the refinement through the revealed aspect of Torah is through it descending and clothing itself in physical matters,
this is a matter of war
[in the manner of the king going out from his place and going to the place of the enemy],
and the true matter of refinement in a manner of rest is in the refinement through the inner aspect of Torah].
